description: Sabotages for win-handles-sys's duplicate_handle_with_access and Access, which were win-sync-sys's duplicate module until DI-14.8.3 moved them. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format.
notCoveredHere: DuplicateHandle's failure other than for a mask Windows refuses is absent: it fails only when the process cannot get another handle, which no test can produce on demand. duplicate.rs says so at the definition. A handle closed twice is not injected for close_handle: the second close would act on a value another thread may have been given, and the sweep would be measuring that and not a test.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: the duplicate ignores the access asked for
sabotages.why: The access is the whole point. A duplicate that gets none cannot be waited on, which the wait tests see, and cannot set, which the modify-state test sees.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: the duplicate keeps the source's access
sabotages.why: DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS (2) makes the call ignore the mask, so every duplicate would be a full-access clone: the narrowing, which is the reason for the function, silently not happening. The synchronize-only tests see it as a set that succeeds.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: the duplicate is inheritable
sabotages.why: A handle that a child process inherits is one the caller did not decide to hand over; the documented contract is that it is not inheritable.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: a refused duplicate is reported as success
sabotages.why: The error path is reached by a mask Windows refuses. Swallowing it would hand back a handle that is not one.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: combining access masks intersects them
sabotages.why: A mask built with | that comes out as the common bits asks for nothing: the modify-state-and-synchronize duplicates cannot set or cannot wait.

sabotages.name: WS-1+.5: the SYNCHRONIZE constant is the modify-state right
sabotages.why: The named right the wait-only handle is built from. Wrong, the handle can set and cannot wait.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the duplicate's failure is tested against 0 rather than FALSE
sabotages.why: The manifest checking itself on the new module: FALSE is 0, so this is an equivalent change on code every duplicate runs. If it comes back caught, something is reacting to text rather than behaviour.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: the query reports no flags
sabotages.why: What the call wrote is the answer; a query that always said none would report every inheritable handle as not.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: the inherit flag is the protect bit
sabotages.why: Each flag is the Win32 bit it is named for; swapped, an inheritable handle would read as protected.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: the protect flag is the inherit bit
sabotages.why: The same for the other flag.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: containing is overlapping
sabotages.why: A set contains another only if it has every flag of it; a set that overlaps it has some.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: combining flags intersects them
sabotages.why: Combining is a union, as for the other masks of this workspace.

sabotages.name: DI-14.8.4: BLIND SPOT: a refused query is reported as flags
sabotages.why: GetHandleInformation fails only for a handle that is not open, which AsHandle rules out, so no test can make it fail. The definition says so.

sabotages.name: WH-1.2: the mask is not passed to the call
sabotages.why: The mask is what names the flags to change: passed as zero, nothing is ever set or cleared.

sabotages.name: WH-1.2: the flags are not passed to the call
sabotages.why: The flags give each flag in the mask its new value: passed as zero, a flag can only be cleared, never set.

sabotages.name: WH-1.2: the mask and the flags are passed in each other's places
sabotages.why: The call takes the mask before the flags; swapped, a flag is set only if it is also what is to be cleared, and a clear changes nothing.

sabotages.name: WH-1.2: a refused call is reported as success
sabotages.why: A failure of the call is its error: a handle the platform refuses, which a test can hold as the current process's pseudo-handle, must not read as set.

sabotages.name: WH-1.2 control: only the flags in the mask are passed as flags
sabotages.why: A control: the platform applies flags & mask, so passing that is the same observable by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
replace: let ok = unsafe { SetHandleInformation(handle.as_handle().as_raw_handle(), mask.0, flags.0 & mask.0) };

sabotages.name: WH-1.2: BLIND SPOT: a bit Windows does not name is narrowed away before the call
sabotages.why: The crate does not narrow what the call is given (HandleFlags), but the platform accepts a bit it does not name and gives it no effect, so a narrowing before the call looks the same from outside. The claim is documented and measured (WH-D-3) and cannot be pinned by a test.

sabotages.name: WH-1.3: the answer is inverted
sabotages.why: TRUE is that the two handles name one object; read the other way, every duplicate is a different object and every pair of different ones is the same.

sabotages.name: WH-1.3: every pair is the same object
sabotages.why: A comparison that cannot say no cannot tell a handle from another object's.

sabotages.name: WH-1.3: no pair is the same object
sabotages.why: A comparison that cannot say yes cannot find a duplicate, nor a handle to the current process.

sabotages.name: WH-1.3: the first handle is compared with itself
sabotages.why: The second handle is the other half of the question: with it dropped, every handle is the same object as whatever it is asked about.

sabotages.name: WH-1.3 control: the call's result is tested against a literal zero
sabotages.why: A control: FALSE is zero, so the same test by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WH-1.4: a failed close is reported as success
sabotages.why: The point of the function is the result a drop throws away: a close the platform refused, which a handle protected from close is, must be an error.

sabotages.name: WH-1.4: the handle is not closed
sabotages.why: A close that does nothing and says it worked leaks every handle it is given; the last handle to a named object is what shows it, since the object is not removed.

sabotages.name: WH-1.4: every close is reported as a failure
sabotages.why: A close that succeeded is Ok: reported as failed, a caller cannot tell a handle that closed from one that did not.

sabotages.name: WH-1.4: the error is not the call's
sabotages.why: The code the call set is the whole of what a caller can learn of why it failed.

sabotages.name: WH-1.4 control: the call's result is tested against a literal zero
sabotages.why: A control: FALSE is zero, so the same test by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WH-2.1: a same-access duplicate gets no access
sabotages.why: DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS with the flag dropped and the mask zero is a handle that can do nothing: a same-access duplicate that cannot wait, which every same-access test sees.

sabotages.name: WH-2.1: an inheritable duplicate is not
sabotages.why: Asking for Inheritable and getting a handle a child does not receive hands the child nothing, silently: the flag read back from the duplicate is how it is seen.

sabotages.name: WH-2.1: the with-access form keeps the source's access
sabotages.why: The wrapper that names a mask must pass it on. Passing Same instead makes every narrowed duplicate a full-access clone, which the synchronize-only tests see as a set that succeeds.

sabotages.name: WH-2.1: the with-access form is inheritable
sabotages.why: The wrapper's documented contract is a duplicate that is not inheritable; the not-inheritable test reads the flag back through it.

sabotages.name: CONTROL: the mask given with the same-access flag is not zero
sabotages.why: DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS makes DuplicateHandle ignore the mask (the page for the call says so), so a nonzero mask beside the flag is the same observable by another spelling. If it comes back caught, something reacts to the text and not to the behaviour.
